title: A scalar string whose text resembles a JSON array turns its parent object into an array
rationale: analyzeStructure inspects VALUES to decide STRUCTURE: any string value under a multi-segment key that looks like a serialized array of more than one element promotes its parent prefix to an array path. Nothing about the input is an array. Note the arity dependence: "[7]" parses to one element and is spared, so fidelity depends on how many commas the user typed.
catchesBugClass: Value-driven structural inference: the entire class of bug where a leaf CONTENT decides its parent TYPE. Any fix must make array detection depend on the flattener own emitted metadata rather than on string shape.
cannotCatch: Requires depth >= 2. At top level the prefix loop never executes, so a flat single-level document round-trips perfectly - a corpus built only from flat documents would show this library as clean.

predicted.detail: The string is destroyed, its characters are retyped as integers, and the enclosing object becomes an array of three synthetic objects.
